preamble: A birthday tribute to 1 across 4 - great writer: thousands of 25s broken! (9,6,3,3,8)

clue.text: They may be jolly good in crew not heading for Wolverhampton

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here good set within the trimmed crew
not tells us to drop a letter from the crew, namely the one named after it

parts.note: a rowing crew is made up of rowers

indicators.note: heading for picks the first letter of the word that follows it, Wolverhampton

explanation.surface: A football-chant tribute to a crew that never sets off for Wolverhampton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not heading for Wolverhampton' removes W from ROWERS to leave ROERS, and 'in' puts G inside. A Jolly Roger is the pirate flag, so the plural fits 'They may be jolly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirate skull-and-crossbones flags are called Jolly Rogers, so these flags may be described as jolly.

clue.text: Men in Fleet Air Arm mostly valuable? They're uncommonly so

indicators.note: in places the men inside the mixed-up letters
fleet in the sense of fast-moving signals letters flying about into a new order
mostly means all but the final letter of the word Arm

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, enlisted men

explanation.surface: Service personnel in the naval air branch are said to be mostly valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet Air Arm' reads as the naval aviation service, but 'Fleet' is the anagram signal, mixing AIR and AR into RARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin plural means rarities, collectables such as books valued because few exist.

clue.text: Regularly pulled out of glossy hat, it's destined for curry!

indicators.note: regularly pulled out of means every other letter is drawn from the words, like a conjuror pulling from a hat

explanation.surface: A magician pulls something from a shiny top hat, something bound for the curry pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The rabbit-from-a-hat picture salutes the honoree's career as a magician; gosht is meat, as in rogan josh dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gosht is the Hindi and Urdu word for meat, typically mutton or lamb, the base of many curries.

clue.text: Hardware ordered right away to provide clue for R? That's frightening!

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to rearrange some tools come with a scary hint for a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes the R; 'to provide clue for R' is a second hint, since the head of raw is R. A rawhead is a bogeyman used to frighten children.
explanation.definitionFit: A rawhead is a nursery bogey, a ghoul told to children to scare them.

clue.text: Respected entertainer starts off, needs lots of paper

indicators.note: off says the letters just named are removed from the following word

parts.note: needs means requires

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of each of the two words Respected and entertainer

explanation.surface: A much-admired performer gets going and calls for a great deal of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Respected entertainer' looks like a description of the honoree, a magician, but only its initials R and E are used: 'starts off' strips them from REQUIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: A quire is a stationery measure of about two dozen sheets, so several of them are a good quantity of paper.

clue.text: Far from dull setter Stephenson initially demoted — it 'ad to be a joke

indicators.note: demoted means sent lower, so in a down answer the letter moves further down

parts.note: the sun is a setter because it sets each evening

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Stephenson
to be a joke implies the letters are made a mockery of and jumbled

explanation.surface: A lively setter, Stephenson, got demoted and thought it must be a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh Stephenson was the paper's crossword editor; 'demoted' moves the S of SUN down to give UNS, and 'to be a joke' turns IT AD into TAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid means sober and dull, so the negated form describes someone lively and unconventional.

clue.text: Flying machines — ten or so — failing to impress lady sawn in half

indicators.note: to impress means to press into, so the half lady goes inside the mixture
failing means going wrong, so the letters are rearranged
sawn in half leaves only the latter half of the word lady

explanation.surface: Some aircraft, around ten of them, fail to wow a woman cut in two by a magician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' scrambles the fodder and 'to impress' presses the back half of the lady into it; ROTONES receives DY. The sawn-in-half lady is a stage illusion, a nod to the honoree's past as a magician.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotodyne is a compound gyroplane, an aircraft with a rotor and propellers, like the Fairey Rotodyne.

clue.text: Escape from sea with minimum of panic — gee, amazing!

indicators.note: amazing means the letters are bewildered into a fresh order
minimum of means the smallest part, the first letter of panic

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a marvellous escape from the ocean without much alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escape from sea' looks like a single picture, but only 'Escape' is the definition, in its sense of a leak.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is the slow leaking of fluid, which is an escape of liquid or gas.

clue.text: Sailor's spirit and extremes of gallantry are staggering

parts.note: grog is diluted rum, the sailor's traditional drink

indicators.note: extremes of means the outermost letters of gallantry

explanation.surface: Navy rum and some heroics leave people reeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unsteady and dazed after drink or a blow is reeling on their feet.

clue.text: Two records rest with singular, amazing puzzler

indicators.note: amazing suggests letters thrown into astonishing disorder and rearranged

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A remarkable puzzle-maker who has broken two records and is taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: The honoree held a world record for the number of crosswords published, which the surface hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: One who composes crosswords sets puzzles, so is a puzzler in the sense of a puzzle maker.

clue.text: Take note of a disappearing card or three — magic!

indicators.note: disappearing tells us the letter a vanishes from the mixed fodder
magic suggests letters conjured into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letter a is the one that disappears

explanation.surface: A conjuror's instruction to watch closely as a card, or three, vanishes by magic.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of OF CARD OR THREE, less an A ('a disappearing'), are rearranged by 'magic' to give FOR THE RECORD; the trick theme salutes a setter who was also a magician.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is on the official log is a way of telling others to note it down.

clue.text: During a break, tackling Crispa's last — and Custos?

indicators.note: tackling means grappling with, so the anagram holds the final letter inside it
break means the letters of During and a are broken up and reassembled
last selects the final letter of Crispa's

explanation.surface: In a pause, a player takes on someone named Crispa and someone called Custos.
explanation.walkthrough: Crispa and Custos were both earlier setters for this newspaper's cryptic, and custos is Latin for a keeper, so the definition doubles as a nod to the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Custos is the Latin word for a keeper or protector, which is what this English word means.

clue.text: A great occasion for 1 across 4 (22), 9 10 11!

parts.note: the cross-references spell out the honoree, his age of eighty, and his job as setter for the paper, and the clue describes his birthday

explanation.walkthrough: The references read Roger Squires (1 across 4), EIGHTY (22), and crossword setter for the Guardian (9, 10, 11): a birthday greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A joyous celebration such as an eightieth birthday is a time of great happiness.

clue.text: Individual approaches entertainment group, getting first part in Crossroads, male part

indicators.note: approaches means comes up to, so the individual sits right beside the entertainment group

parts.note: poll means a head, an individual counted
ENSA was the British wartime body that entertained the troops

indicators.note: first part in picks the opening letter of Crossroads

explanation.surface: A single person heads for a troupe and lands a first role in the soap Crossroads.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossroads was a long-running British TV soap opera set in a motel, so 'part' here looks like an acting role.
explanation.definitionFit: In a flower the stamen is the male organ, and its anther contains this pouch of pollen.

clue.text: One of Squires' d___ French team went ahead, after sacking editor

parts.note: the blank stands for a word beginning with this letter, which supplies it
onze is French for eleven, the size of a football or cricket side

indicators.note: after sacking means once the named person has been dismissed from the word

parts.note: went ahead means led

explanation.surface: One of the squires has been left blank, while a French side went in front after firing its editor.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank 'd___' hints at a squire's word starting with D and supplies that letter; ONZE needs two steps, French then the size of a football side. A donzel was a young squire seeking knighthood.
explanation.definitionFit: A donzel is an archaic term for a young squire not yet knighted, one of the class of squires.

clue.text: Man, say, appearing on Monday — many beguiled

indicators.note: appearing on means coming after, so the island follows the day

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an example of an island
D is the Roman numeral for 500, many

explanation.surface: A man, apparently, shows up on a Monday and charms a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man, say' is not a person: it is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beguiled is to be deceived or led astray by charm, the past participle of mislead.

clue.text: Having kittens, lacking time to get out

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letter for time is removed

parts.note: having kittens is British slang for being very anxious, in terror

explanation.surface: A cat giving birth needs to get out without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having kittens' is British slang for being in a panic, not a cat giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: If a calculation is out, it is wrong, mistaken.

clue.text: Everyone that's in Dr Who is a playful type?

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the abbreviation for doctor

parts.note: taken as the letters written
all means everyone
IE stands for id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Everyone involved in the TV show Doctor Who is a fun-loving sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dr Who' reads as the TV show, but only DR works; 'Who is a playful type?' asks for the one who dallies.
explanation.definitionFit: One who dallies flirts, toys or dawdles, a frivolous trifler.

clue.text: Group do something for this splendid fellow

parts.note: a class is a group or category
to act is to do something

explanation.surface: A gang takes action in honour of a fine chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of real quality and style is informally called this; the phrase praises someone excellent.

clue.text: Future flier, no gentleman to treat with disrespect

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably
to dis is slang for to show disrespect

explanation.surface: A would-be pilot, being no gentleman, insults others.
explanation.walkthrough: The caddis is the larva of the caddis fly, so it will fly in future.
explanation.definitionFit: The caddis worm is an aquatic larva that turns into an adult caddis fly.

clue.text: An adventurous chap like Vespucci, I become trapped under a foreign sea

indicators.note: trapped under means placed below, so in this down entry the pair goes after

parts.note: mer is French for sea
go can mean become, as in go mad

explanation.surface: A Vespucci-like explorer finds himself pinned beneath a foreign sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Amerigo Vespucci was the Italian explorer after whom America is said to be named.

clue.text: Awful to-do — sailor leaving Oscar in a flap

indicators.note: awful means dreadful, so the letters are put into disorder
leaving means the sailor is taken out of the word Oscar

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A dreadful fuss as a sailor walks out on Oscar, leaving everyone in a flap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a flap' looks like panic, but 'a flap' is the definition, a small pet door.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hinged opening lets a pet come and go, so this hatch is a flap.

clue.text: Pretty girl in crimson rose

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: crimson is a shade of red
a belle is a beautiful young woman

explanation.surface: A lovely girl dressed in a crimson rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the flower in a picture of a girl in red; it is the verb, past tense of rise, meaning revolted.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise up against authority is to revolt, so rose in that sense means revolted.

clue.text: Point out momentous number!

indicators.note: out says the compass point is removed from the following word

parts.note: momentous means weighty
W is the compass point west

explanation.surface: Someone stresses that a big figure is a significant one, here the honoree's age.
explanation.walkthrough: The honoree was turning eighty, which makes the number momentous in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight tens make up this figure, a cardinal number.

clue.text: Excellent setter appearing finally in Attenborough film (a third cut)

indicators.note: in puts the final letter of setter inside the shortened film title
a third cut means one third of the film title's letters are removed

parts.note: Richard Attenborough directed the 1982 biopic of the Indian leader

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of setter

explanation.surface: A fine setter shows up at last in an Attenborough movie, trimmed by a third.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand is an informal word for splendid or very good.

clue.text: "Tap it twice", said Roger — not a bad magician!

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the letters are put into a scrambled order
twice means the word it is used two times over

parts.note: the letter a is removed as the clue says not a

explanation.surface: Roger tells someone to tap it twice, calling it a decent conjuring trick.
explanation.walkthrough: TAP, IT, IT, SAID and ROGER, less the A ('not a'), are rearranged by 'bad'; 'not a bad magician' also praises the honoree, a former magician.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestidigitation is sleight of hand, so one who practises it is a conjuror or illusionist.

clue.text: See 10
He occupies hearts, getting more mature

parts.note: H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts
older means more mature

explanation.surface: Someone takes over people's affections and grows older in doing so.
explanation.definitionFit: One who has or occupies a post, title or property is its owner or tenant.
